title: Meaning of M8 by 1
answer_text: M8 by 1 means a metric thread with a nominal diameter of 8 millimeters and a pitch of 1 millimeter.
caution_text: That is different from the M8 coarse pitch of 1.25 millimeters.
question_examples: What does M8 by 1 mean?||Is M8 by 1 the same as a normal M8?

title: Same diameter but different pitch
answer_text: Do not combine screws that share a nominal diameter but have different pitches.
caution_text: Forcing them together can damage the threads.
question_examples: Will an M8 fit even if the pitch is different?||Can I mix the M8 1.0 and the 1.25?
match_keywords: fit||mix||combine||different pitch||pitch is different||same diameter||will it go in||interchange

title: Metric versus inch threads
answer_text: Do not treat metric and inch threads as interchangeable even when the diameters look close.
caution_text: Check the standard and the pitch and do not force the screw in.
question_examples: Can I use an inch screw that is close in diameter?||Do metric and inch threads match?

title: Machine screw versus tapping screw
answer_text: A machine screw goes into an existing tapped hole or nut. A tapping screw forms its own thread in a pilot hole.
caution_text: Confirm the pilot hole and mating material that suit the screw type.
question_examples: What is the difference between a machine screw and a tapping screw?||Can I use this tapping screw in a normal nut?

title: Tool for a socket head cap screw
answer_text: A socket head cap screw takes a hex key or hex bit of the matching size.
caution_text: Confirm the tool size against the part specification.
question_examples: What tool turns this socket head cap screw?||Which driver do I use on a hex socket head?
source_title: NBK about socket head cap screws

title: Choosing a socket for a bolt
answer_text: Choose a socket that matches the across flats size of the bolt head and the drive square of the torque tool.
caution_text: Do not decide the tool size from the nominal diameter alone. Check the part specification.
question_examples: How do I pick the socket size?||Which socket should I use on this bolt?
source_title: Tohnichi across flats and drive square

title: Strength grade from the head marking
answer_text: A head marking such as 8.8 is the clue for identifying the strength grade of a steel bolt.
caution_text: If there is no marking or it cannot be read, check the part number or the work order.
question_examples: What does the number on the bolt head mean?||How do I read the head marking?
match_keywords: head marking||stamped||8.8||10.9||strength grade||number on the head

title: Lubrication and clamp load
answer_text: Oil or grease changes the friction, so do not reuse a dry tightening torque as it is.
caution_text: Check the process standard or the specified value for that part.
question_examples: Is the torque the same if there is oil on it?||Does grease change how tight I go?

title: Mating material and tightening conditions
answer_text: When the mating material is aluminium or plastic, do not reuse the tightening conditions used for steel.
caution_text: Check the process standard that covers the mating material.
question_examples: Does the torque change for aluminium?||Is it the same on plastic?

title: Washers and bearing surface
answer_text: Washers and the shape of the bearing surface affect friction, so tighten with the combination that was specified.
caution_text: Do not add or remove washers on your own.
question_examples: Does a washer change the torque?||Can I tighten it with this washer stack?

title: Torque asked from the diameter alone
answer_text: The specified tightening torque cannot be determined from the nominal diameter alone.
caution_text: If the process, part, head marking and surface condition cannot be identified, do not proceed with tightening.
question_examples: How many newton meters do I use?||What torque should I set?
match_keywords: how many newton||what torque||how tight||torque setting

title: Tap drill conditions
answer_text: To decide the tap drill hole, confirm the nominal diameter and the pitch of the thread.
caution_text: Give priority to the in-house machining standard including the method and the mating material.
question_examples: How do I decide the tap drill?||What pilot hole do I drill before tapping?

title: Pilot hole for a tapping screw
answer_text: A tapping screw pilot hole is decided from the screw type, the mating material, the plate thickness and the engagement length.
caution_text: Check the manufacturer guideline table or the process standard.
question_examples: What pilot hole for this tapping screw?||What hole do I drill in this plate?

title: Pilot hole too large
answer_text: If the pilot hole for a tapping screw is too large, the pull out strength drops and the joint can loosen.
caution_text: Do not proceed with an out of specification hole. Check the machining standard.
question_examples: The pilot hole looks a bit big, is that ok?||Can I carry on with this oversized hole?
match_keywords: hole too large||too big||oversized||loose in the hole||pull out

title: Pilot hole too small
answer_text: If the pilot hole for a tapping screw is too small, the driving torque rises and the joint can be defective.
caution_text: Do not force the screw in. Check the machining standard.
question_examples: The pilot hole looks small, is that ok?||It is hard to drive in, is the hole too small?
match_keywords: hole too small||too tight a hole||hard to drive||undersized

title: Unusually stiff from the start
answer_text: Stop work for now. The pitch may be wrong, the screw may be cross threaded, or there may be debris.
caution_text: Do not force it in. Check the condition of the screw and the tapped hole.
question_examples: It is stiff right from the start.||Something is wrong as I start the screw.
match_keywords: stiff from the start||hard from the beginning||tight straight away||cross thread

title: Stainless screw galling
answer_text: Stop work for now. The stainless screw may be galling or seizing.
caution_text: Do not force it round. Contact your supervisor.
question_examples: The screw suddenly stopped turning.||It has jammed halfway in.

title: Screw spins without tightening
answer_text: Stop work for now. The thread or the mating material may be damaged.
caution_text: Do not tighten further. Check the screw and the mating material against the replacement criteria.
question_examples: It keeps spinning and never tightens.||The screw will not do up.

title: Whether a screw can be reused
answer_text: Whether a screw may be reused cannot be decided as a blanket rule.
caution_text: Check the part number and the reuse criteria for the process. If there is no criterion, fit a new screw or ask your supervisor.
question_examples: Can I use this screw again?||Is it ok to refit the screw I took off?
